- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–8% for 2–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add upward bias to forecast by 2–6% for 3–7 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; if below, overcorrects upward — adjust by -10% to +10% depending on deviation from MA.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true volatility; increase forecast by 1–4% if sentiment is volatile or event-driven (e.g., policy change, auction results).
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.7, -0.5, +0.7), model tends to lag in direction change; adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
- When true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day average, model is likely misaligned with sentiment; re-calibrate using sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day history.
